findings.issue: The new canonical English Psalm 92 file has <tei:pb n="23" facs="…n76"/> just before chapter 92. But page 23 (s77-b0) opens with the end of Psalm 33 ('May Thy grace … for Thee.'), and that page break belongs with the documentary Psalm 33. This file is not transcluded by the English index, and the pb sits outside the chapter-92 scope, so nothing compiles wrongly. Still, the English project now has a second marker for page 23 in the wrong place. Likewise, canonical en/ashrei.xml repeats morning_ashrei.xml's pb n=25.
findings.fix: Remove the pb from en/psalm_92.xml. Optionally keep the en/ashrei.xml pb only if it's intended to show where the page breaks inside the expanded transclusion, and record that this is deliberate.

findings.fix: Look at the enlarged s78-b2/b3 clusters. Apply the same ruling if the shape matches; otherwise leave as is. This is not a new linguistic question.

findings.issue: Openers such as <tei:milestone unit="chapter" n="84"/> carry @n but no @corresp. Under scope rule 3 that makes them terminators, not openers. This follows the convention the repository already uses, and it changes no resolved range.
